subject.title: Feature: Per-spawn tool restrictions for sub-agents

question: Should `sessions_spawn` expose an enforced per-call allowlist for native sub-agents, and should unsupported ACP or CLI-backed runtimes reject that parameter rather than ignore it?
rationale: This model-facing API defines a security and session-state contract: maintainers must choose the permanent policy-composition semantics and supported runtime boundary before the candidate implementation can land.

options.title: Approve narrow allow-only policy
options.body: Accept a per-call allowlist that can only intersect existing permissions, persists with the child capability envelope, and fails clearly on unsupported runtimes.

options.title: Require named agent profiles
options.body: Decline dynamic restrictions and require callers to spawn preconfigured least-privilege agent identities instead, closing the candidate implementation and documenting that boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow allow-only policy
recommendation.body: Accept a per-call allowlist that can only intersect existing permissions, persists with the child capability envelope, and fails clearly on unsupported runtimes.

likelyOwner.reason: They posted the latest maintainer-facing assessment and are the strongest available routing signal for the cross-cutting spawn API and security decision.
